statement.p: Resolve the following vectors into components:
(a) The vector \vec v in 2-space of length 7 pointing up at an angle of \pi/6 measured from the positive x-axis.
(b) The vector \vec w in 3-space of length 5 lying in the yz-plane pointing upward at an angle of 3\pi/4 measured from the positive y-axis.

static.solution:
(a) The components are v_1 = 7 \cos \pi/6 = (7)({\sqrt 3\over 2}) = {7\sqrt 3 \over 2} and v_2 = 7 \sin \pi/6 = (7)({1\over 2}) = {7 \over 2}. Thus \vec v = {7\sqrt 3 \over 2}\,\vec i + {7 \over 2}\,\vec j.
(b) Since the vector lies in the yz-plane, its x-component is 0. Its y-component is (5)(\cos 3\pi/4) = -{5 \over\sqrt 2}, and and its z-component is (5)(\sin 3\pi/4) = {5 \over\sqrt 2}. So the vector is \vec w = -{5 \over\sqrt 2}\,\vec j + {5 \over\sqrt 2}\,\vec k.
